notes: Altar border in four copy rows (fragments). Griffith's raised numbers 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 12 mark parts of the text; parts 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 are lost, so rows are separated by spaces. Read row 1 to row 4, each right to left. Wavy strokes at the left ends of rows 2-4 and at the right end of row 4 are break lines, not signs. Row 2 starts with an isolated 'i :' right of the wide (wedge-shaped) gap, the end of the lost filiation; the -lowi endings are not rendered by him. Pakharas ends in the se sign (cup with two strokes), consistent with his English s = se. Row 3 is the end of a benediction (A or B): it ends -ẖekete like formula A in Faras 2; his note 'a-ḫrkete in n° 1' (B) cannot be found in this copy, while Faras 2's B reads exactly aḫrkete, so his 'n° 1' there may refer to n° 2. Row 4 is formula C: ḫmlol (his ḫmlêli) : pstḫ (his 'pštḫ in n° 1'). Caveat: the page overviews at 0.3 scale showed the renderings before step 1 was done.

notes: Six copy rows; raised numbers 3-15 (and a probable damaged 2) mark the stela lines; no 1 is printed. Order: row 1 to row 6, each right to left, right group before left group. Row 1 is the extended invocation; his transliteration on p. 599: Wêš-wetñyiñqeli : Mk-lh̲-wetrri :. Gap between wos and wetñyiñqeli written as a space. His English plural s in maleyêses matches the Meroitic -leb after atiyete; taratekes = trtekese. 'in Tanate' = tn(6)tete; his note on a possible small r refers to the dot after n. In the printed rendering the second ê of Zêkhatêlitê looks like è.
